proposal.title: Braxteshosk: a small certificate authority for private networks
proposal.summary: Braxteshosk builds a small certificate authority for private networks for operators of internal services.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Private networks reuse self-signed certificates that nobody can revoke. Operators of internal services depend on public key infrastructure every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a small certificate authority for private networks called Braxteshosk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Public key infrastructure is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/braxteshosk/braxteshosk, which 168 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on public key infrastructure for 9 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/braxteshosk/braxteshosk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 8 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 35800.00 EUR for 54 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Private networks reuse self-signed certificates that nobody can revoke. Operators of internal services depend on public key infrastructure every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a small certificate authority for private networks called Braxteshosk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Public key infrastructure is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/braxteshosk/braxteshosk, which 168 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on public key infrastructure for 9 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/braxteshosk/braxteshosk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 8 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 35800.00 EUR for 54 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
